title: Series connection
body: A series connection is one in which any charge passing through one circuit element must proceed through all elements in that connection and has no other path available, so the current in each element is the same.
ced_evidence: 11.5.A.1.i: "A series connection is one in which any charge passing through one circuit element must proceed through all elements in that connection"

title: Parallel connection
body: A parallel connection is one in which charges may flow through one of two or more paths, and the potential difference is the same across each path.
ced_evidence: 11.5.A.1.ii: "A parallel connection is one in which charges may flow through one of two or more paths"

title: RC time constant
caution: Only qualitative use is required: τ is the time for a charging capacitor's charge to reach about 63% of its final value, or for a discharging capacitor's charge to fall to about 37% of its initial value. Students are not expected to model charge or current mathematically as functions of time.
ced_evidence: 11.8.B.1.i: "The time constant of an RC circuit is a measure of how quickly the capacitor will charge or discharge"; 11.8.B.1.ii–iii (63% / 37%)
